model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route, net debt zero)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (4.2% 5y) is less than half the bonus-adjusted EPS CAGR (8.5% 5y) and revenue CAGR (7.6% 5y): Bradesco has distributed most of its earnings (JCP + dividends) and absorbed IFRS 17 / OCI marks, so book growth understates franchise growth. Revenue 5y CAGR selected, cross-checked against 2026 loan-growth guidance of 8.5-10.5%.
historical_growth.notes: All figures from IFRS 20-F annual series in Metrics.csv. EPS CAGRs are BONUS-ADJUSTED: reported EPS was not restated for the ~10% bonus share issues of 2017-2022, so EPS is re-derived as net income / FY2025-equivalent share count (FY2020 shares 8,835.5m x 1.1 x 1.1 = ~10,690m vs 10,642m reported FY2022), giving FY2020 EPS R$1.49 vs FY2025 R$2.24. Reported EPS (1.88 -> 2.35) would show 4.6% and is not comparable. FCF CAGRs are null: operating cash flow for a bank swings with deposit and loan flows (FY2023 -178, FY2025 -62,534) and is not an owner cash flow. FY2022 net income is the IFRS 17-restated figure. FY2023 is a provisioning trough (credit impairment 30.2bn incl. Americanas), which flatters the 3-year-from-FY2022 numbers less than the 5-year.

scenario_narratives.base: The turnaround keeps grinding forward: loans grow at the guided 8.5-10.5% in 2026 and fade toward nominal GDP, the cost-to-income ratio keeps improving from 46.5% but short of the 40% target, and higher credit costs from a stretched Brazilian household and SME sector absorb part of the efficiency gain. Recurring ROAE settles around 17%, a point above a 16% BRL cost of equity, so Bradesco is worth a little over book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Transformation delivers: the efficiency ratio hits ~40% by 2028, Bradesco Seguros (ROAE ~23%) and Bradsaude keep growing above guidance, Selic falls toward 11% by 2027 easing credit costs, and secured lending (now ~61% of the book) keeps NPLs contained. ROAE converges toward Itau's ~20%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Brazil's credit cycle turns: elevated Selic and household debt-service burdens push NPLs and provisions higher (Q1-26 credit costs already +27% y/y), Nubank/Inter/Mercado Pago keep taking retail fee and deposit share, John Deere Bank/agri delinquency adds noise, and recurring tax-program charges recur. ROAE slips to ~14%, below the cost of equity, so growth destroys value and the bank is worth less than book.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Bradesco is valued as a bank: free cash flow to equity (recurring net income less the capital retained to grow book in line with revenue) discounted at a BRL cost of equity, with no net-debt deduction because deposits are operating funding. Values are computed in BRL and translated at spot USD/BRL to USD per ADR (1 ADR = 1 preferred share). The question the model answers is whether recurring ROAE (~16-17%) sustainably exceeds a ~16% BRL cost of equity; at today's price (~1.1x book) the market is pricing roughly that.
key_risks_to_valuation: BRL/USD: a 10% move in the real moves the USD IV 10% with no change in the business.
Cost of equity: at ROAE close to CoE, value per share is highly sensitive to the BRL discount rate (see sensitivity grid).
Unmodelled R$10bn capital increase: dilutive if priced well below intrinsic value.
Recurring vs reported earnings gap: tax-program and other 'non-recurring' items have recurred (Q1-26 R$1.8bn).
Credit cycle: NPL 90d 4.3% and rising, Q1-26 credit costs +27% y/y.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2.98-4.30. BRL=X and BBDC4.SA from the same API for the FX parity check.
data_sources.financials: Metrics.csv (IFRS 20-F annual FY2015-FY2025); 6-K managerial earnings releases Q3-25..Q2-26 for TTM recurring revenue, recurring net income, shareholders' equity, CET1 and 2026 guidance (BBD_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt lines 66-82, 365-388); ADR ratio from BBD_Annual_FY2025.txt:18012.

inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero market: Bradesco discloses no share-based compensation expense on the 20-F cash flow statement (EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year); executive variable pay is cash/profit-sharing inside personnel expense, already in the flow.
inputs.fx_note: BRL->USD at 1/5.2223 (Yahoo BRL=X, USD/BRL 5.2223 at 2026-10-02T22:10Z). ADR ratio 1 ADS = 1 preferred share (FY2025 20-F: 'Each preferred share ADS corresponds to one preferred share', BBD_Annual_FY2025.txt:18012). Parity check: BBDC4.SA local close / 5.2223 lands within 1% of the BBD ADR close on 2026-10-02, confirming the rate direction and the 1:1 ratio. The rate is not moved by refresh_price.py; re-date it on the next refresh.
inputs.share_count_basis: 10,577.0M total shares (common + preferred, ex-treasury) per FY2025 20-F; no dilutive securities, no SBC. Held flat. Common (BBDC3) and preferred (BBDC4) are treated as equal economic claims; preferred are entitled to a 10% higher dividend, so per-preferred value is understated by at most ~5%. The proposed capital increase of up to R$10bn (2Q26 release p.23, pending regulatory approval) is NOT modelled: terms, price and share count are undisclosed in the extracted filings; a subscription near intrinsic value is roughly per-share neutral.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 16.0% in BRL, single rate across scenarios (risk charged once, in the rate; scenarios carry the credit/macro risk in margins). Built from the flows' own currency: long NTN-B real yield ~7% + IPCA expectations ~4% gives a ~11% long-run nominal BRL risk-free (spot BM&F fixed rate 14.11%, Selic 14.25% at Jun-26, Bradesco's own forecast Selic 13.75% end-2026 / 11.00% end-2027), plus beta ~1.0 x 5% ERP. Terminal growth 5% nominal BRL (~4% inflation + ~1% real). Entry hurdle 17% in BRL = the house 15% USD hurdle grossed up for the ~2pp BRL-USD inflation differential (1.15 x 1.04/1.025 - 1 = 16.7%).
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: bank flow is net income to common; lease cost already inside administrative expense.
inputs.nci_treatment: Recurring net income is attributable to Bradesco shareholders (after minority shares, incl. Bradsaude NCI post-May-2026 listing and 50% John Deere Bank); nothing further deducted.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine (precedent NAB.AX, USB, WFC, TFC, HBAN, NTRS, STT). SKILL.md routes banks away from owner-FCF: deposits are operating funding, not debt, so net_debt = 0 and OCF (R$-62.5bn FY2025) is meaningless. Engine mapping: revenue = managerial total revenue (NII + fees + insurance/pension/capitalization result), TTM to Jun-26 = 35,008 + 35,978 + 36,808 + 37,477 = R$145,271m; 'ebitda_margin' = PRE-TAX recurring margin, backed out of recurring net income (TTM 6,205 + 6,516 + 6,811 + 7,050 = R$26,582m, 18.3% of revenue) at a 24% effective tax rate (FY2025 cash taxes 7,637 / implied pre-tax ~31,300; JCP interest-on-equity deductibility keeps it below the 45% statutory bank rate); D&A, SBC, working capital = 0; 'capex' = capital RETAINED to grow book equity in step with revenue = (equity/revenue 175,230/145,271 = 1.206) x g/(1+g), so the flow is FCFE = NI - retention. Retention uses total book equity rather than CET1 (prudential deductions of R$44bn, largely DTAs, grow with the book), which is deliberately conservative given CET1 11.3% and management's pending R$10bn capital increase. Managerial (BR GAAP recurring) basis chosen over the IFRS 20-F (FY2025 IFRS revenue NII+non-II 118,744, NI 23,673) because the quarterly releases carry both numerator and denominator on one basis; FY0 TTM equity R$175,230m (Jun-26 managerial). last_fcf = recurring NI 26,582 less equity growth Jun-25->Jun-26 (175,230 - 167,312 = 7,918) = 18,664. Q1-26 reported NI (5,030) was R$1.8bn below recurring on tax-program items; the bear margin path allows for such recurring 'non-recurring' tax charges.

bear.ebitda_margin_path_note: Credit-cycle hit: cost of credit up (as Q1-26's +27% y/y), recurring tax-program charges, digital fee erosion; NI margin ~16-17%, ROAE ~14% - below the 16% cost of equity, i.e. the bank destroys value on retained capital.

base.ebitda_margin_path_note: Pre-tax recurring margin. 24.1% = TTM recurring NI margin 18.3% / (1 - 0.24). Rises to 25.6% (NI margin 19.5%, ROAE ~17%) as the cost-to-income ratio keeps falling from 46.5% toward the mid-40s, partly offset by a higher cost of credit (NPL 90d 4.3% and rising).
base.capex_pct_path_note: Retention, not capex: 1.206 x g/(1+g), keeping equity/revenue constant.
base.growth_rates_note: Year 1 9.5% = mid-point of 8.5-10.5% loan-growth guidance with Q2-26 revenue +10.3% y/y; fades to 5% nominal BRL.

bull.ebitda_margin_path_note: Efficiency ratio reaches ~40% by 2028 as targeted; NI margin ~21.7%, ROAE ~19-20% (Itau-like).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: credit costs are rising into a high-Selic economy, CET1 at 11.3% needed a proposed R$10bn capital increase, and Brazilian sovereign/political risk sits on top. Base 50% on ten straight quarters of recurring-profit growth. Bull cut to 25% because it needs the 40% efficiency target AND a benign credit cycle at once.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

diagnosis.detail: Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: regulatory single point of failure
Projected growth 7.6% exceeds the through-cycle revenue CAGR 6.0%

sanity_check.fix_applied: Sanity check flagged implied P/E 1.6x (vs a 10yr average of 0.4x) and P/B 0.21x (vs a 10yr max of 0.10x). Investigation traced this to a BRL/USD currency-direction bug in the sanity checker's own historical-multiple calculation (scripts/sanity_check.py), not a defect in the valuation: it converts the USD ADR price the wrong way before comparing against BRL financials, understating every historical multiple by roughly the square of the FX rate. No change was made to the DCF model. Recomputed by hand and denominated consistently in BRL, the base case implies about 7.3x trailing recurring earnings and 1.1x book value -- both inside Bradesco's normal historical range (see implied_multiples_after_fix) -- so the valuation itself is not the problem; the checker's currency handling is. Fixing that checker is a separate, cross-ticker change out of scope for this run.

implied_multiples_after_fix.note: Computed directly from valuation.base.intrinsic_value_brl x shares_outstanding against BRL trailing recurring financials (TTM to Jun-26), bypassing the checker's historical_table() currency bug.
implied_multiples_after_fix.basis: Recurring TTM net income R$26,582m, TTM-Jun26 book equity R$175,230m, TTM revenue (NII+fees+insurance) R$145,271m
implied_multiples_after_fix.assessment: Within Bradesco's plausible historical range (~6-13x P/E, ~0.8-2x P/B for Brazilian bank majors); the sanity-check trip does not reflect a real valuation problem.
